title: Private Money, Private Minds
subtitle: This week in Bitcoin & Nostr news

topics.title: Live Dashboard & Market
topics.description: Price stalled on an oil spike; ETFs had their best week in a year

slides.heading: Live Dashboard
slides.body: Where Bitcoin sits right now. The full dashboards:

slides.heading: Market: Price Stalled, the ETFs Didn't
slides.body: A flat-to-down week on the chart. Underneath, the biggest ETF buying in almost a year.
bullets: Sep 28: Bitcoin slipped ~1.7% to about $83K. Oil went back above $100 after Trump rejected Iran's terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Gold and silver fell too
Meanwhile, spot ETFs took in $2.4B in the week ending Sep 25, their biggest week since October 2025. IBIT $1.2B, FBTC $702M
That flipped 2026 ETF flows positive: +$934M for the year, after sitting ~$5.8B in the red on July 13
Analysts credit the Treasury's plan to buy back more long-dated bonds
Saylor kept stacking: Strategy bought 1,665 BTC at ~$85,681, now 847,666 BTC
slides.linkLabel: The Block: ETFs turn positive for 2026

topics.title: Shielded Bitcoin
topics.description: A proposal for Zcash-style private payments on Bitcoin with no soft fork

slides.heading: Shielded Bitcoin: Private Payments, No Soft Fork
slides.body: Sep 24: researchers at [alloc] init published a plan to hide who paid whom, and how much, on Bitcoin itself.
bullets: Authors: Clara Shikhelman, Misha Komarov, Aleksei Moskvin
It borrows Zcash's design: encrypted notes, zero-knowledge proofs, and "nullifiers" that stop double-spends without revealing which coin moved
No rule change: shielded transactions ride inside normal Bitcoin transactions as tagged data ("shbtc:" in OP_RETURN or the witness)
Indexers, programs anyone can run, read the chain, check the proofs, and ignore anything invalid
The week's most-discussed thread on Delving Bitcoin

slides.heading: Shielded Bitcoin: The Catch, and a Regulator's Nod
slides.body: The hard part isn't in this paper yet: getting real BTC in and out.
bullets: Locking and releasing actual BTC is left to a follow-up paper on "PIPEs v2", a scheme that unlocks a key only when a valid proof shows up
Goal: no federation, no custodian. Until that paper lands, it's a design, not a product
Same week, SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce's farewell speech (Sep 23, "Looking for Change in Haystacks"): collecting ever more customer data makes crime harder to find, not easier
Her fix: zero-knowledge proofs, so a bank can confirm you passed a check without keeping your documents
Question for the room: would you use a privacy layer that lives outside Bitcoin's rules?

topics.title: Local AI Meets Bitcoin & Nostr
topics.description: Run the model yourself, pay for AI with sats, give agents wallets with limits

slides.heading: Local AI: Not Your Model, Not Your Mind
slides.body: Same idea as "not your keys, not your coins." If the model runs on someone else's server, they see every prompt.
bullets: Sep 17: Bonsai 2 27B, a strong open model squeezed to 5.9 GB. It keeps 98.2% of the full model's benchmark score. Runs on a Mac, iPhone, or iPad
Apache 2.0 license, reads text and images, and it's free to download
Ollama, the easiest way to run models at home, shipped three releases in September
Umbrel's app store has Ollama and Open WebUI: local AI on the same box as your node
Sep 24–25: HRF and NED's AI Hack for Freedom. HRF's advice to activists: run the model on your own device so prompts never leave it

slides.heading: Local AI: Pay for Models With Sats, No Account
slides.body: Some models are too big for a laptop. The Bitcoin answer: pay per question, with no sign-up.
bullets: Routstr: an AI marketplace where providers are listed on Nostr and paid in Cashu ecash, topped up over Lightning
Got a spare GPU? Run a Routstr node and sell your own model's answers for sats
Sep 26: the Sovran ecash wallet now pays Routstr per request, straight from your balance. It shows each provider's price and a privacy rating
Sep 24: Block brought Lightning to x402, the web standard for AI agents paying for things. Google, AWS, Coinbase, Visa, and Mastercard are members
Spiral's Steve Lee: "Agents will make billions of small payments." Now some settle in sats

slides.heading: Local AI: Agents Get Keys and Wallets, With Limits
slides.body: Once an agent can pay, the question is how much it's allowed to spend.
bullets: Sep 23: Bray 3.5, a tool that lets AI assistants use Nostr, added wallet guardrails: a cap per payment, a daily budget, and a human confirm before spending
Keys stay in a separate signer (NIP-46), so the agent never holds your nsec
Nymbot: an AI assistant you message over encrypted Nostr DMs. No email, no card, pay with Lightning. Cloud models, but no account
Sep 19: the NostrAgent paper proposes a standard for agent identity, delegation, and Lightning payments on Nostr
Question for the room: would you hand an agent a wallet connection with a $5-a-day limit?

topics.title: Core 32 & a Lightning Patch
topics.description: Bitcoin Core 32.0 is in final testing; Core Lightning users should upgrade now

slides.heading: Core 32 & a Lightning Patch: Upgrade Season
slides.body: Two things for node runners, one of them urgent.
bullets: Bitcoin Core 32.0 is at release candidate 2. The final release is targeted for Oct 10
What's new: faster block validation, better fee estimates, and PSBT version 2 as the default in several wallet commands
It also fixes a command-execution flaw in certain wallet setups. Testers wanted: rc2 is out now
Urgent: Core Lightning 26.06.8 is a security release. Upgrade now. The tests are held back for a while so attackers can't copy them
Further out: a working post-quantum Lightning prototype (Optech #424). The cost: nodes download ~10x more data

topics.title: FIPS Watch
topics.description: v0.5.2: a security release every node should install

slides.heading: FIPS Watch: v0.5.2, Every Node Should Upgrade
slides.body: Sep 28: a maintenance and security release. No network format change, so nodes can upgrade one at a time.
bullets: A privacy leak closed: nodes using Nostr to get through home routers signed some messages with their routing key. That tied their identity to those messages on every relay
Windows: any user on the machine could read or plant the node's key. The installer now locks that folder down
Gateway: any device on the LAN could exhaust its address pool. Now capped and rate-limited
A security update to the TLS library its relay connections use
New: RPM packages for Fedora-style Linux. Still pre-audit, as always

topics.title: Nostr This Week
topics.description: Iris calls, smarter relays, three NIPs merged, and our own relay

slides.heading: Nostr This Week: Calls, Relays, and New NIPs
bullets: Iris Chat (Sep 24): voice and video calls, even over a local network with no internet
nostream 3.1: relays can now raise or lower their spam proof-of-work automatically as traffic changes
NIPs merged: NIP-39 identity proofs now cover Bluesky and Discord. NIP-86 adds relay invite codes. NIP-51 moves follow sets to a new kind
Our own relay: every heart on these slides is a Nostr reaction stored on our Buzz relay. Tap the topics you liked

topics.title: Clarity Act: The Champions Leave
topics.description: Tillis, Lummis, and Peirce are all heading out

slides.heading: Clarity Act: The Champions Are Leaving
slides.body: Two weeks after the 49–50 vote that stalled it, the bill is losing the people who carried it.
bullets: Sen. Thom Tillis is not seeking re-election and steps down at year's end
Sen. Cynthia Lummis, the lead author in the Senate, isn't running again either
SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce, head of the crypto task force, leaves this Friday, Oct 2
What's left: talk of reviving it in the lame-duck session after the midterms. No date
Why it matters to us: the next bill gets written by people who haven't been in this fight
slides.linkLabel: Who leads the Clarity Act next?

topics.title: Builder Spotlight
topics.description: Super Testnet's lilp2p: browser-to-browser chat, with Nostr only as the introduction

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: Super Testnet's lilp2p
slides.body: No new Bitcoin code from Super in September, so here's one from February we never covered.
bullets: What it is: a tiny JavaScript library (~240 lines) that lets two web browsers talk to each other directly
The trick: the introduction runs over encrypted Nostr messages through any relay, using throwaway keys
After the handshake the relay drops out. Messages go browser to browser over WebRTC
Honest limit: strict firewalls can block the direct link, and there's no fallback server yet
Try it: one person clicks "Set up comms", the other scans the QR. Public domain (CC0). I forked it to help build it out

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Run an AI model on your own computer tonight, then unplug the internet

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Run an AI Model on Your Own Computer
slides.body: Ten minutes, free, and your prompts never leave your machine.
bullets: Install Ollama from ollama.com (Mac, Windows, Linux)
In a terminal: ollama run gemma4:e2b. It's a small model built for laptops, a few GB to download
Ask it anything. Then turn off Wi-Fi and ask again. Still works: that's the point
No terminal? Ollama and Open WebUI are one-click installs in Umbrel's app store
Bring back one thing it got right and one it got wrong
